info.name: SMemories - notes
info.description:
Collection links for friends' notes (T-012) and public note submission (T-034), on the v2 contract since T-068 (`/api/note-collection/*`, `/api/public-collect/*`, `{status,data}` envelope, `ERROR_*` codes, Unix ms timestamps): create, list, revoke, the public lookup and the multipart note form (the link token is the query parameter `token` of the submit route). Run against an API started with SMEM_ENV=dev.

Setup, once per database: the owner endpoints need a verified email, and the dev mail is only printed to the API's stdout, which Newman cannot read. So the collection uses three fixed accounts (A, B verified, C never verified): run `newman run postman/notes.postman_collection.json --folder "Setup (once per database)"`, then `make verify-newman-users` (marks A and B verified in the dev database; for another database run `UPDATE user_tab SET email_verified_at = UNIX_TIMESTAMP(NOW(3)) * 1000 WHERE email IN ('newman-notes-a@example.com','newman-notes-b@example.com')`). After that run the whole collection as often as you like: Setup tolerates accounts that already exist (409, or 429 once the register limit of 5 per hour per IP is used up) and everything else only logs in. Run it in order: Edge cases reuses the users and the yearbook of the Full flow, and ends by deleting the yearbook. Run it from the postman/ directory (`newman run notes.postman_collection.json --working-dir .`) because the note requests upload the photo fixtures of fixtures/media/ (and the Setup command above then needs the same flags). The public routes count only misses (unknown tokens) against 60 per IP per 15 minutes, and a run makes about 8 of them; submissions are limited to 100 per IP per hour, a run makes about 14, so run the whole collection at most 6 times an hour from one address or run `make reset-limits`. Each run creates its own links, so it can run twice back to back.

item.name: Full flow

exec: // Once per run, before the first request: a deadline a week ahead for the main link.

item.name: 1. Login A
2. Login B
3. A creates a yearbook
4. A creates a link (label is NFC-trimmed; the token is shown here)
5. A lists: one link, no token or hash anywhere
6. Public lookup, no cookie - 200

exec: pm.test('body', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data).to.eql({yearbook: {title: 'Newman notes book'}, owner: {display_name: pm.collectionVariables.get('nameA')}, deadline_at: Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('deadline')), open: true, fields: pm.response.json().data.fields}));

pm.test('form fields', () => { const f = pm.response.json().data.fields; pm.expect(f.map(x => x.id + ':' + x.required)).to.eql(['name:true', 'relationship:false', 'message:true']); pm.expect(f[0]).to.have.keys(['id','kind','label','hint','required','max_length']); pm.expect(f[2].kind).to.eql('long_text'); });

item.name: 7. Public lookup while B is signed in - same answer, B's session is ignored
8. A creates a second link (no label, no deadline)

exec: pm.test('empty label, null deadline, a different token', () => { pm.expect(c.label).to.eql(''); pm.expect(c.deadline_at).to.eql(null); pm.expect(c.token).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('linkToken')); });

item.name: 9. A revokes the first link - 200
10. Revoking again - 200
11. Lookup of the revoked token - 404
12. Lookup of an unknown token - 404, the same answer

exec: pm.test('same message as for a revoked token', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error_message).to.eql('not found'));

item.name: 13. A lists: newest first, the revoked one has revoked_at
14. A creates a link that expires in 2 seconds

exec: // a deadline (Unix ms) that is still in the future when the request arrives

item.name: 15. Lookup after the deadline - 410 ERROR_COLLECTION_CLOSED

exec: const end = Date.now() + 3200; while (Date.now() < end) {} // wait for the deadline to pass

item.name: 16. Friend sends a text-only note - 200, only the id comes back

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); pm.test('only the id', () => { pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('OK'); pm.expect(Object.keys(b.data)).to.eql(['id']); pm.expect(b.data.id).to.match(/^[0-9A-Z]{26}$/); });

item.name: 17. Friend sends emoji, Vietnamese text and two photos - 200

formdata.value: {"name":"Newman Friend","relationship":"classmate","message":"Chúc bạn mãi vui 🎉👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 ❤️ Nguyễn Văn Ánh\n\nHẹn gặp lại!"}

item.name: 18. A bot fills the honeypot - 200 as if stored (nothing is)
19. A lists the links: the two real notes are counted, the bot's is not
